_description: f3_anchor41M's geometry with NO LONGITUDE HOLDOUT: 576x10, 8 heads, d_dec 768, d_z 64, patch 3, family-3 0.25 deg North Atlantic monthly, 60,000 steps at batch 512 — identical to f3-anchor-41M in every architectural field, and differing from it in exactly one: holdout_lon '0,0', so the -45..-25 block trains instead of being withheld. WHY '0,0' AND NOT 'none': [0,0) is the empty half-open interval, so the mask is bit-identical to what 'none' produces — but TWELVE eval scripts under ml/ still re-read ck['args']['holdout_lon'] as `float(v) for v in ...split(',')` (ablate_channels, dip_check, probe_head, probe_kfold, probe_sequence, project_amoc, recon_decoder, recon_eval, rollout, rollout_spatial, train_joint, trainprobe). A codec whose args say 'none' trains fine and then loses its ENTIRE probe ladder and every later eval to `ValueError: could not convert string to float`, each raise swallowed by a best-effort guard — a green run with an empty probe archive. train.py accepts 'none' and warns loudly about exactly this; the recipe passes the form that works end to end. Routing those twelve readers through train.lon_holdout_mask is the follow-up that makes 'none' safe, and it includes ml/rollout_spatial.py, whose roll is the primary instrument. That single difference is the experiment. Consequences to know before reading its numbers: the anomaly transform's z-score statistics are now taken over ALL longitudes of the train years, so this codec's input normalisation is NOT the anchor's, its weight hash is new, and its embedding cache is a fresh entry rather than a hit on the anchor's. DISPATCH WITH `resume` EMPTY — this is a fresh codec and there is no no-holdout parent to continue from; a recipe cannot pin resume (the seed step reads inputs.resume in an `if:`, a YAML expression context $RECIPE_RESUME cannot reach), so `resume` is the one field the dispatch still has to get right. `steps` 60000 is the anchor's own total budget, not a guess. HEAD_PROBE IS 'true' HERE EXPLICITLY (2026-08-21). The workflow's default is now true as well, so this key changes nothing about what runs — it states it, because a recipe is the record of a configuration that was RUN and 'which read-out produced the verdict' is now part of that configuration. ml/CLAUDE.md §3: unpooled is the verdict, the pooled ridge is a labelled legacy comparable, and both sides of a comparison switch together (the head's raw-3x3 and wind-only bars are fitted in the same loop, scripts/probes_run.sh).
_provenance: Geometry and step budget read off the f3_anchor41M__pixelmae.pt release asset itself (2026-08-19, §0.1 — the pickle's own `args`, not ml/recipes/f3-anchor-41M.json and not memory): steps 60000, batch 512, lr 3e-4, d_z 64, patch 3, d_model 576, n_layers 10, n_heads 8, d_dec 768, mask_ratio 0.5, holdout_years '2009,2017,2023', holdout_lon '-45,-25', anomaly true; top-level step 60000, tag run-80. The anchor itself is run-62/run-63 (40,692,849 params), tagged run-80. The holdout_lon change is Chris's decision of 2026-08-19: the per-pixel anomaly transform already removes location-memorised climatology, the block costs 25% of the training pixels, and it confounds the spatial-coupling claim because about half the stencil head's measured advantage is earned patching the hole in its own coords=(lat/90, lon/180) feature. NOTHING HAS BEEN RUN AT THIS CONFIGURATION YET — this recipe is the dispatch surface for that run, and its _provenance becomes a measurement when the run lands.
